newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Islamist PM Erbakan close to resigning.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Islamist PM Erbakan close to resigning.

text.p: Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, was close to quitting on Wednesday in an attempt to defuse a bitter row with the secularist army.
A spokesman for Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party said the prime minister would visit President Suleyman Demirel later in the day to give in his resignation.
"Yes, he will probably go there at 1800 (1500 GMT)," Welfare Party spokesman Salih Kapusuz said when asked by Reuters if Erbakan would take his resignation to the presidential palace.

Erbakan announced earlier this month that he would step down under a plan to transfer power to coalition ally Tansu Ciller, who would head a caretaker government to take the country to early elections.
But the prime minister had not fixed a date for resigning.
The government, set up a year ago, has slowly been crumbling under pressure from the powerful military since February.
Welfare believes it can come back from early elections with a greater mandate to boost the role of Islam in public life.
Turkish newspapers said Ciller's True Path Party would pull out of the battered alliance if Erbakan did not step down by the end of the day.

"We have given Welfare until 2400 (2100 GMT). This is our last date and we will give no concessions on it. If Erbakan doesn't resign we will do what is needed," the Hurriyet daily quoted True Path senior MP Mehmet Golhan as saying.
Other True Path officals confirmed the threat.

The prime minister, 70, did not mention resigning in an hour-long speech to his MPs on Tuesday. "Welfare is working with all its might for democracy and human rights. If sacrifices are necessary, it will make them willingly," he told his MPs.
He would have to give his resignation to President Suleyman Demirel but the president's office said on Wednesday there was as yet no meeting with Erbakan on the president's schedule.
Army pressure has hindered Erbakan's goal of introducing Islamist reforms and building bridges to Turkey's Moslem neighbours.

The generals, who have staged three coups since 1960, say their fight with religious activism is a matter of "life or death" for Turkey, a secularist nation with ambitions of joining the European Union.
Erbakan presided at the weekend over the founding summit in Istanbul of the Developing-Eight (D-8) Moslem nations.

But he has been helpless to stop growing military ties with Israel that have angered the Arabs. Five Turkish navy vessels docked in an Israeli port on Monday in defiance of the prime minister's pro-Arab stance.
Parliament must approve a power transfer and early polls but a string defections from Ciller's wing has cost the ruling alliance its majority in the 550-seat assembly.
A far-right powerbroker has said he would back government efforts to push the coalition's plans through parliament.
Support from rightist leader Muhsin Yazicioglu's eight MPs would give the government 282 deputies on paper, enough to win approval if they can hold on to their own restive MPs.
